title: Understanding Your Menstrual Cycle
description: A comprehensive guide to understanding the four phases of your menstrual cycle and what to expect.
detailSubtitle: Understanding your cycle isn’t just science — it’s a form of self-love and emotional awareness.
content:
Your menstrual cycle is not just something that happens once a month — it affects your body every single day. It changes your energy, mood, skin, cravings, confidence, and even the way you think.

When you understand your cycle, you learn how to work with your body, not against it. And that is one of the most empowering things a girl can do.

✨ The Four Phases of Your Cycle
1. Menstrual Phase — Period Days
During this time, your hormones drop, and your body needs rest, warmth, and gentleness.

2. Follicular Phase — Fresh Start
Your energy rises, your mind clears, and you feel more creative and motivated.

3. Ovulation — Confidence Peak
You feel social, active, and glowing. Best time for big tasks and workouts.

4. Luteal Phase — Slow Down
You may experience PMS, cravings, or mood shifts. Your body is preparing for your next cycle.

🌷 Why It Matters
Knowing your phases helps you understand your emotions, energy, and needs. Your body isn’t confusing — it’s communicating with you.
author: 🩺 Dr. Meenakshi Gupta

title: Mental Health & Yoga Cycle
description: Discover how yoga and mindfulness can help manage PMS symptoms and improve overall well-being.
detailSubtitle: How movement, breathwork, and mindfulness help you find emotional balance through your cycle.
content:
Your mental health and hormones are deeply connected. Every phase of your cycle affects the way you feel.

✨ Follicular Phase — Feel Good Phase
You feel motivated, focused, and emotionally lighter.

✨ Luteal Phase — Sensitive Phase
You may feel anxious, irritated, or emotional — not because you're weak, but because your hormones are shifting.

✨ Yoga & Mindfulness
Slow breathing calms the nervous system. Gentle yoga reduces cramps and stress. Meditation helps emotional control.

✨ Movement Doesn’t Need to Be Hard
Sometimes the best workout is stretching, breathing, or a slow walk.

🌷 When you move with your cycle, you feel calmer, more in control, and deeply connected with your body.
author: 🩺 Dr. Meera Sharma

title: Stress Management Techniques
description: Effective strategies to manage stress and maintain emotional balance throughout your cycle.
detailSubtitle: Simple, science-backed ways to calm your mind and body.
content:
Food isn’t just fuel — it’s therapy for your hormones. Eating according to your cycle improves mood, skin, cravings, and period pain.

❤️ Menstrual Phase — Comfort
Warm soups, dals, leafy greens, jaggery, and herbal teas support you.

🌱 Follicular Phase — Fresh Energy
Your body loves fruits, smoothies, salads, oats, and yogurt.

✨ Ovulation — Glow Phase
High-fiber foods, lean proteins, and antioxidants support your peak strength.

🍫 Luteal Phase — Craving Phase
Dark chocolate, bananas, nuts, and warm meals help reduce bloating and irritation.

Cycle syncing is not dieting — it’s self-care through food.
author: 🩺 Dr. Kavya Nair

title: Nutrition During Your Cycle
description: Learn about the best foods to eat during different phases of your cycle.
detailSubtitle: Support your hormones, energy, and mood with mindful eating.
content:
Food is therapy for your hormones. Eating right for each phase gives you stable mood, better energy, clearer skin, and fewer cravings.

❤️ Menstrual Phase
Warm, iron-rich foods bring comfort and strength.

🌱 Follicular Phase
Fresh, colorful foods help you feel renewed.

✨ Ovulation
Proteins and fiber support your peak energy.

🍫 Luteal Phase
Magnesium-rich foods ease PMS symptoms.

Cycle syncing makes your body feel supported, understood, and balanced.
author: Nutritionist Ananya Rao

title: Exercise and Your Hormones
description: Learn how to adjust your workout routine to work with hormonal changes.
detailSubtitle: Sync your workouts with your natural flow.
content:
Your workout doesn’t need to be the same every day — because your body isn’t the same every day.

❤️ Menstrual Phase — Rest
Light stretching, yoga, and slow walks.

🌱 Follicular Phase — Fresh Start
Strength training, pilates, cycling.

✨ Ovulation — Power
HIIT, running, dancing, heavy lifting.

🌙 Luteal Phase — Slow Down
Moderate workouts, yoga, long walks.

Following your hormonal rhythm makes fitness easier, more enjoyable, and more effective.
author: Fitness Coach Priya Singh

title: Sleep and Hormonal Balance
description: Understanding the connection between sleep and your hormones.
content:
Sleep is one of the best ways to support your hormones. Poor sleep increases PMS, stress, cravings, and irregular cycles.

🌙 Luteal Phase Sleep Problems
Many girls feel restless, hot, or emotional.
A calming bedtime routine helps.

☁️ Deep sleep improves:
Mood
Stress levels
Hormonal balance
Energy
Focus

A well-rested girl is more confident, stable, and peaceful.
author: 🩺 Ganesh Mehta

title: Managing PMS Naturally
description: Natural remedies and lifestyle changes to help manage PMS.
detailSubtitle: Gentle habits that make PMS easier.
content:
PMS doesn’t mean you’re overreacting — it means your body needs care.

Helpful habits:
Warm herbal teas
Magnesium-rich foods
Gentle walks and yoga
Mindful breathing
Avoiding too much caffeine

PMS teaches self-awareness and emotional strength.
Your body isn’t against you — it’s communicating.
author: 🩺 Arpit Singh

title: Hormonal Acne Solutions
description: Understanding and treating hormonal acne with care.
content:
Hormonal acne is not a flaw — it’s your body reacting to hormonal changes.

✨ What helps:
Gentle cleansers
Salicylic acid
Niacinamide
Tea tree
Consistent routines

Lifestyle matters too:
Hydration
Good sleep
Balanced meals
Stress control

Your skin doesn’t define you — patience and care heal it.
author: 🩺 Dr. Aarohi Mehta
